bull.t: Growing QCaaS adoption and production usage
bull.b: Subscription growth and a rising share of production applications indicate customers are moving beyond experimentation. This can support more recurring revenue, deepen customer integration and improve monetization of D-Wave’s cloud, software and hybrid solver ecosystem.

bull.t: Backlog and enterprise traction are expanding
bull.b: A substantially larger backlog and multiple live enterprise deployments improve revenue visibility and validate commercial use cases. Measurable operational benefits can support renewals, broader deployments and reference-account momentum across telecom, healthcare and other industries.

bull.t: Technical validation supports a differentiated dual-platform strategy
bull.b: Peer-reviewed hardware validation strengthens credibility for D-Wave’s gate-model roadmap while its annealing platform already serves production workloads. Maintaining both approaches could broaden the addressable market and reduce dependence on a single quantum architecture.

bear.t: Persistent operating losses and negative cash generation
bear.b: Sustained cash burn and widening operating losses mean growth currently requires substantial investment without internally generated funding. This raises dependence on external capital, limits financial flexibility and increases execution risk before the business reaches scale profitability.

bear.t: Revenue remains volatile and dependent on system deliveries
bear.b: Large, irregular system transactions create uneven revenue recognition and make quarterly performance dependent on delivery and installation timing. Until recurring cloud and services revenue becomes larger, this volatility can obscure underlying demand and complicate planning.

bear.t: Lower margins and rising personnel costs pressure scalability
bear.b: The margin decline and heavier staffing expense show that commercialization and product development are consuming significant resources. Unless revenue scales faster than these costs, operating leverage may remain weak and the path to sustainable profitability may extend.
